description: Composite figure mixing one SEM fractograph with two TEM micrographs of H90 (Fe-8Mn-6Al-0.2C) low-density steel after tensile deformation. (a) is a secondary-electron SEM fractograph (instrument bar: HV 20.00 kV, mode SE, det ETD, mag 2 000 x, WD 8.3 mm, vac mode High vacuum, 6/23/2017 3:16:36 PM, Quanta FEG; 50 µm scale bar) annotated with white text boxes and red arrows marking "the herringbone crack", "the river pattern", "secondary crack" and "dimples"; the surface is rough with flat cleavage-like facets, tear edges, short curved river patterns and few small dimples, i.e. quasi-cleavage. (b) is a bright-field TEM micrograph with a 200 nm scale bar showing two dark, heavily dislocation-populated regions separated by a sharp boundary, both labelled "δ-F" — the δ-ferrite dislocation morphology. (c) is a TEM micrograph with a scale bar at bottom left (value illegible) in which red dashed outlines mark a dotted circle labelled "retained austenite" and an elongated ladder-shaped lath labelled "martensite"; the field shows dense tangled dislocation contrast. Together the panels argue that fracture is quasi-cleavage while high-density dislocations retained in ferrite and martensite, plus residual austenite, support the TRIP-assisted strengthening.

subfigures.description: SE-SEM fractograph of H90 steel (2 000 x, 20.00 kV, WD 8.3 mm, 50 µm scale bar, Quanta FEG). White labels with red arrows mark 'the herringbone crack', 'the river pattern', 'secondary crack' and 'dimples' on a rough surface with flat cleavage facets and tear edges.
Bright-field TEM micrograph of the region near the fracture, 200 nm scale bar, showing two dark heavily dislocated regions separated by a sharp boundary and both labelled 'δ-F' (δ-ferrite).

TEM micrograph with a red dotted circle labelled 'retained austenite' and an elongated red dashed-outlined lath labelled 'martensite'; dense tangled dislocations fill the matrix. Scale-bar value at bottom left is not legible.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a secondary-electron SEM fractograph acquired at mag 2 000 x, 20.00 kV, WD 8.3 mm, high vacuum on a Quanta FEG instrument, with a 50 µm scale bar.
In (a) red arrows point to four explicitly labelled fracture features: 'the herringbone crack', 'the river pattern', 'secondary crack' and 'dimples'.
The fracture surface in (a) consists of flat cleavage-like facets with tear edges, short curved river patterns and only a few small dimples, i.e. a quasi-cleavage morphology.
Panel (b) shows two dark, dislocation-dense regions separated by a sharp boundary, and both regions carry the label 'δ-F'.
Panel (b) carries a 200 nm scale bar at the lower left.

Panel (c) marks a small dotted red circle labelled 'retained austenite' and a larger elongated red dashed-outline region labelled 'martensite' within a matrix showing dense, tangled dislocation contrast.

The caption identifies (a) as the fractograph, (b) as dislocation morphology in ferrite and (c) as dislocation morphology in martensite, and states the figure is of H90 steel after tensile deformation.

The citing text states that Fig. 5a shows quasi-cleavage fracture features under different solution treatment conditions, with flat cleavage facets, micropores, tear edges, secondary cracks and a few dimples.
The citing text attributes the ductile fracture area mainly to austenite deformation and the quasi-cleavage area mainly to ferrite deformation.
The citing text states that a small amount of austenite remained after the strong TRIP effect during tensile deformation in Fig. 5b and c.
The citing text asserts that high-density dislocations were observed in both ferrite and martensite, which enhances mechanical properties.

The citing text proposes that martensite formed inside austenite grains acts as a barrier to dislocation glide, a site of dislocation accumulation and a source of partial dislocations, restricting dynamic recovery and dislocation climbing.
